_: Which generated 3D models and which catalogue photos are allowed near the AR view.
_why: build.ts used to accept a real GLB on one test: does the file exist. Every model under assets/3d
was reconstructed by an image-to-3D provider from the SKU's position-1 photo, and the manifest
records the consequence on 21 of 28 of them: 'judge skipped - no vision assist wired'. Nothing
The provider is faithful to its input and its input is often not the product. Image roles are
assigned by POSITION, not content (stages.ts: `const role = IMAGE_ROLES[i]`, and
validate-curated.ts enforces it), so every SKU in the catalogue reads 1:hero 2:angle 3:in_context
4:detail 5:pack_or_dimensions whatever the pictures actually show. Position 1 is called the hero
whether it is the product, its carton, a rival brand's bag, or a WiFi router.
So there are two decisions to record per SKU, and neither can be computed from the data as it
stands: is the MODEL the product, and is the PHOTO the product. Both were made by rendering every
GLB at the AR view's own camera and looking at all 135 catalogue images. Absence from a block
means accepted. Re-check this file whenever assets are regenerated - and delete an entry rather
than leaving a stale reason behind it.
This is a holding position, not a fix for the catalogue. The images themselves are still wrong
and want re-sourcing; until then a parametric model at the SKU's real dimensions is the honest
thing to draw, and it is what a rejection falls back to.

models.BUL-HAV-LEDPLUS9WB22: The model is the retail carton. Image 1 is the Havells 9W box with the bulb printed on its face, so that is what came back - a cuboid wearing box artwork.
models.BUL-WIP-GARNET9WB22: The carton again, with two loose bulbs fused to it. Image 1 is the Wipro Garnet box beside its contents.
models.CEM-ACC-SP50: Degenerate: a few floating fragments and unreadable text, no bag. Nothing here is a 50 kg sack.
models.CEM-AMB-PLUS50: A rival brand's bag. Image 1 for this SKU is a Dalmia sack, and the model wears Dalmia's blue and yellow livery on an Ambuja SKU - the exact thing isRivalHost() exists to stop, arriving as geometry instead of as an image.
models.EPX-FOS-CONBEXTRAEP10: Degenerate: floating text and a small cube.
models.EPX-PID-EPOXYINJGROUT: A human hand holding a bottle. The source photo is a hand demonstrating the nozzle and the reconstruction kept the hand.
models.FIR-NEW-CA-EB-01: A portable extinguisher, but this SKU is an extinguisher CABINET (CA-EB-01) - the images are right and the model is of the wrong object.
models.TIL-SOM-T31F119001859102: A human figure. The five source images are all clean tile faces, so this is the provider failing on its own, which is the reason a gate has to exist at all rather than only better inputs.
models.TST-TOP-GM-52: A dark crate. The Topcon GM-52 is a total station; this is its shipping case at best.
models.SOL-VIK-PARADEA-550: Judged 0.00 against its own source photograph, same_product=false — "a completely different object, a surrealist artistic sculpture". Twice: the first attempt embossed a human figure across the panel (0.34). A flat rectangular module gives single-image photogrammetry no depth cue to work from, so the provider invents one. The parametric framed module at 1134 x 2278 is the honest picture.

photos._: Derived — do not hand-edit. SKUs whose photographs must not texture a parametric model, with what the vision pass saw. Regenerate with `npx tsx services/pipeline/tools/classify-images.mts --write`.
photos.EPX-FOS-CONBEXTRAEP10: no bare, single, correctly-branded unit on a clean ground among 5 images — #1 other_product, #2 lifestyle_or_stock, #3 other_product, #4 other_product, #5 product_in_packaging
photos.GLS-AIS-EDGE-NATURAPLUS: no bare, single, correctly-branded unit on a clean ground among 5 images — #1 lifestyle_or_stock, #2 lifestyle_or_stock, #3 lifestyle_or_stock, #4 lifestyle_or_stock, #5 lifestyle_or_stock
photos.GLS-GUA-CLIMAGUARD-BLUE5: no bare, single, correctly-branded unit on a clean ground among 5 images — #1 lifestyle_or_stock, #2 lifestyle_or_stock, #3 lifestyle_or_stock, #4 lifestyle_or_stock, #5 lifestyle_or_stock
photos.GLS-SGB-SUNBAN-SAPPHIRE5: no bare, single, correctly-branded unit on a clean ground among 5 images — #1 lifestyle_or_stock, #2 other_product, #3 lifestyle_or_stock, #4 lifestyle_or_stock, #5 other_product

photo_positions._: Derived — the position that actually shows the product. Not position 1 by default: that is the assumption this replaces.

decisions._: Judgements a person made, as opposed to the derived blocks above. These are not gaps waiting to be filled.
decisions.GLS-AIS-EDGE-NATURAPLUS: Glass is a MATERIAL, not an object, and there is no photograph of it to find. AIS, Guardian and Saint-Gobain all photograph glass as architecture — a facade, a partition, a room — because a 5 mm clear pane on a white sweep is invisible. Guardian offered fourteen candidates and all fourteen were buildings. The parametric pane at 1200 x 1800 x 5, tinted and blended at alpha 0.35, is the honest model, and unlike the others it is not a compromise: it is what the product looks like.
decisions.GLS-GUA-CLIMAGUARD-BLUE5: As above. Sourcing a 'product photo' here would mean adopting an architectural scene and calling it a pane.
decisions.EPX-FOS-CONBEXTRAEP10: Sourced candidates all fail on something other than the pack rule — the available Conbextra EP10 photographs put the base and hardener on a dark or busy ground rather than a clean one, so a cut-out is not possible. The parametric two-part kit stands until a studio shot turns up. Not refused for being packaging; the pack rule already admits that.
